candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel limit types (instream waste concentration formulas, domestic/chronic/human-health derived limits, and separate use-specific criteria columns). Which column or formula is treated as the enforceable discharge limit for a given parameter and use determines the numeric limit selected for compliance comparison.

Acute aquatic instream waste limits are expressed as a function of effluent concentration Ce. Interpreting blank Ca/Ce cells versus the tabulated zero in the 2.13*Ce column changes whether Ce is treated as zero, unknown, or not applicable, which changes the computed limit and whether a numeric comparison can be made.

MQL is listed as a per-pollutant reporting/detection attribute. Whether MQL defines a minimum quantitation threshold for enforceable comparison, a monitoring obligation, or only a method characteristic affects limit applicability, monitoring requirement evaluation, and how sub-MQL or missing results are classified.

This pollutant row omits an MQL value while other listed pollutants include one. Whether the blank MQL means no quantitation requirement, inherited default, or incomplete data changes whether monitoring was required and how missing or non-detect evidence should be interpreted.

Many criteria cells use 1E+100 instead of a finite limit. Treating this as no enforceable numeric limit (report-only) versus a literal very large limit changes whether compliance comparison is applicable and how absent or non-numeric results are categorized.

Every listed pollutant shows N/A in the Need TMDL column. Interpreting N/A as no TMDL-based limit applies versus status unknown affects whether a TMDL-related numeric limit is in scope for discharge-limit selection.

This row pairs finite acute (19), chronic (15), and human health (30) criteria with 1E+100 placeholders in other columns and zero derived instream values. Which of these columns is operative for a given discharge/use determines the enforceable numeric limit used in exceedance evaluation.

The segment groups pollutants under a BASE/NEUTRAL heading distinct from prior rows. Whether this label limits applicability to certain analyte classes or monitoring suites affects which parameters are in scope for limit and monitoring-obligation evaluation.

Ambient and effluent concentration inputs are column headers for values that are blank in every row while derived columns show zeros. Whether blanks mean zero concentration, not required, or missing evidence changes limit derivation and missing-evidence classification for those parameters.
